name: D.I.G.G.L.E. (comedy)
source: elizita, a joke one: our own persona script. Uses the same in-browser sentence model as tiers 4 and 5 (Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, Apache-2.0).
about: This one is a joke. D.I.G.G.L.E. stands for Distinctly Infrastructure-Grade, Genuinely Load-bearing Engineer. He is a frontend engineer. He will tell you he is full-stack. He will tell you that a lot.

Under the joke it's the most advanced rule set here, because it uses everything the engine can do at once: AIML-style patterns, ELIZA-style reflection ("I need a holiday" → "You need a holiday? I could build that"), topics spotted anywhere in a sentence (say "database" or "Docker" and he gives himself away), a follow-up question remembered with <that> (say yes when he offers to show you his backend), facts about you ("my dog is called Rex", "I use Python") and matching by meaning when no pattern fits exactly.

He also has three moods, judged by the sentence model the way PARRY's were. Telling him he's "just frontend" raises his defensiveness; compliments raise his smugness; mentioning production outages or asking him to fix the server raises his panic. The levels pick which version of a reply he gives, and push defensiveness or panic to 18 and he logs off.
As in every tier, the model never writes a word. It only picks which human-written rule to use, and the workings under each reply show how.
